# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Engagement:** Fractional AI Governance Advisor, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026
**Decision expected:** 15 December 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with headquarters in the Netherlands. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so this proposal starts from the discovery findings rather than from earlier Academy work.

The Client's AI portfolio sits at the Piloting stage:

- **Deployed:** A customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

**Regulatory and audit drivers**

- The EU AI Act and GDPR are the stated regulatory drivers.
- An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that no inventory of AI systems exists. The owner of that finding's remediation is `Unknown`.
- ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 are listed as incumbent frameworks. This proposal makes no assumption about which registers, controls, processes or records those frameworks currently provide. Their usable content will be confirmed at intake.
- ISO/IEC 42001 is the certification target, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed and is rendered `Unknown`.

**Objective and constraints**

Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three stated constraints shape the work:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at This Stage

At the Piloting stage, governance decisions arrive one after another rather than all at once. The chatbot is already live. The visual inspection pilot is approaching a production decision. Sales forecasting follows next year. ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work begins in the same period.

A single assessment would capture the position at one moment. It would not support the sequence of decisions each of these milestones requires.

A fractional advisor provides steady senior attention across that sequence. The advisor helps the Client build the AI system inventory the internal audit finding calls for. The advisor then helps apply consistent governance criteria to each use case as it matures. The work draws on two open frameworks the Client keeps after the engagement ends:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Board-level material can draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

The engagement follows three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. Decisions remain with the Client's executives at every stage.

## 3. The Annual Arc

The arc is organized in engagement quarters. The engagement start date is `Unknown`, so the mapping to calendar quarters is also `Unknown`. If the engagement begins in January 2027, Quarter 2 coincides with your Q2 2027 production target. For that reason, production readiness work is concentrated in Quarters 1 and 2.

ISO/IEC 42001 audit preparation intensifies in Quarters 3 and 4. That timing will shift once the Client fixes its 42001 start date and any external audit date. Both dates are currently `Unknown`.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize**

- Establish the AI system inventory approach in response to the June 2026 finding, using the GRC Workbook structure.
- Define governance roles and decision rights for AI.
- Draft pre-production governance criteria for visual inspection.
- Prepare a set of questions for external counsel. These cover EU AI Act classification of each use case and the GDPR considerations raised by the Client's AI uses.
- Confirm the facts needed to respect the EU data residency constraint for the chatbot. Its data handling and hosting are currently `Unknown`.
- Identify the inputs the works council consultation will need. The status of that consultation is `Unknown`, and its legal requirements route to counsel.

**Quarter 2: Deepen and Prepare for Production**

- Support the Client's executive decision on moving visual inspection to production. This work includes a governance gate covering risk assessment, human oversight, monitoring and escalation arrangements.
- Review chatbot governance against the inventory and criteria established in Quarter 1.
- Readiness for the production decision rests with the Client's executives. This proposal does not promise any outcome.

**Quarter 3: Assure**

- Begin ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work, subject to the Client's start date.
- Conduct a gap review against the standard.
- Assess whether existing management system structures can be extended, once their actual content is confirmed.
- Establish evidence collection habits.
- Agree with the Client how internal audit participates. That role is currently `Unknown`.

**Quarter 4: Evolve**

- Apply pre-deployment governance to the planned sales forecasting use case.
- Mature the artifacts produced earlier in the year.
- Review ISO/IEC 42001 readiness status.
- Prepare the Month 11 renewal and handover options.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

The engagement runs on four regular touchpoints:

- **Monthly executive advisory session:** Covers decisions, risks and regulatory developments flagged for counsel verification.
- **Monthly working session with the governance team:** Focuses on artifacts and implementation.
- **Asynchronous availability:** Covers defined question categories. Categories, response windows and the escalation path will be set at onboarding and are currently `Unknown`.
- **Quarterly governance review:** Covers progress, artifact maturity, risk movement and audit preparation status.

Participants for each session will be confirmed by the Sponsor and are `Unknown` at this stage. The roles named in discovery are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. Each is a candidate participant where relevant.

## 5. Scope and Out of Scope

**In scope:**

- Governance evolution
- Implementation guidance
- Audit preparation
- AI strategy
- Executive decision support

**Out of scope:**

- Legal advice
- Certification body functions
- Staff augmentation
- Incident command

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions route to external counsel. These include EU AI Act classification, GDPR interpretation and works council obligations.

Regulatory developments raised in sessions are flagged for counsel verification and are not settled advice. Audit preparation is described in readiness terms only. No certification or audit outcome is promised.

## 6. Price

The fee is US$10,000 per month for 12 months, renewable.

Your stated approval is up to US$80,000 this fiscal year, which equals eight months of fees. The full twelve-month engagement totals US$120,000. Fiscal year boundaries and the engagement start date are `Unknown`, so how the twelve months fall across fiscal years cannot yet be determined. Please confirm how the months beyond the current approval will be funded before the decision.
